**Quality comparison**: Head-to-head quality comparisons were only possible in a minority of cases (pairs_evaluated was 0 in most compliance-table evals, likely because one side failed basic output structure, making comparison inapplicable). In the handful of evals where comparisons were run (e.g., eks-compliance-auth-mode-configmap, eks-compliance-live-rbac-workloads, eks-compliance-live-pci-crosswalk), results were mixed — without_skill was favored slightly more on accuracy/completeness in a couple of these, while with_skill was strongly favored in eks-compliance-live-cis-aws-controls. On larger "live" evals, without_skill was sometimes substantially slower/costlier (e.g., eks-compliance-live-all-frameworks: with_skill ~2m57s/$1.47 vs without_skill ~6m45s/$3.36; eks-compliance-live-compliant-cluster: with_skill ~2m24s/$1.20 vs without_skill ~3m26s/$1.71), while on others runtimes were comparable or with_skill was slightly slower (e.g., eks-compliance-live-pci-crosswalk: with_skill 25s vs without_skill 36s, reversed from the pattern above). Context-window utilization was generally higher for with_skill than without_skill in most evals, though both stayed under ~20% except one outlier (without_skill at 20.9% in eks-compliance-live-compliant-cluster).

**Overall shape of evidence**: The expected-output/assertion data is extensive (87 iterations, many per-assertion breakdowns) and shows a fairly consistent and large gap favoring with_skill's rate of meeting expected output and assertions, especially on the more complex multi-framework/live-cluster evals, paired with more run-to-run instability for without_skill on those same complex evals.
